Messages.Author: Ray Powers
Messages.Body:
Ok, sorry, one more total newbie question:

If I understand the rules correctly, If I have a 10 strength vampire in my
inactive pool, I need to put TEN blood from my pool onto this guy to make
him active. That's 1/3 of my blood right there!!!

My question is this, once I make him active, can I then pull a couple
blood back into my pool, and send him hunting to make up the deficit. And
if I take the blood back, does he go back to being inactive?

Thanks again!

Messages.Author: Shane Hamish William Travis
Messages.Body:
Ray Powers (ra...@ramp.com) wrote:
: If I understand the rules correctly, If I have a 10 strength vampire in my

: inactive pool, I need to put TEN blood from my pool onto this guy to make
: him active. That's 1/3 of my blood right there!!!

You understand correctly. This is why some players play with a lot of
little (2-4) vampires and no big ones at all. Thing is, the big ones
have the votes and some cool powers... It is a trade-off each player must
decide on their own.

: My question is this, once I make him active, can I then pull a couple

: blood back into my pool, and send him hunting to make up the deficit. And
: if I take the blood back, does he go back to being inactive?

No. There are cards which allow you to do things like this however;
Blood Doll - Master card, played on a vampire of yours. Allows you to move
one blood per turn either from your pool to the vampire or from the
vampire to your turn.
Minion Tap - Master Card, one-shot. Remove blood from a vampire (up to a
maximum of all the vampire has) and put it in your blood pool.

There are others, but these are both common and you are more likely to
have one of these if you just started playing...

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
pap...@fc.hp.com (Bob Ellison) writes:

>Yup yup yup. 10-capacity vampires are cool - but there's quite a cost.
>This is what makes Jyhad work better than Magic. In Magic, the rarer
>cards are usually more powerful than the commons, and are thus preferred.
>In Jyhad, the rare cards are powerful - but at a price that balances
>the effect.

Not that capacity 10 vamps are any rarer than other vamps. You just
don't see as many come out :-).

In general, though, the rare cards in Jyhad are just more interesting, not
game-unbalancing as in Magic (as you said). Sometimes the reverse is
true. The Chainsaw is on the Uncommon sheet (twice), while the (in
every way superior) Sawed-off Shotgun is on the Common sheet.

Having a chainsaw in combat may be more "interesting" but the mechanics
of the game favor the shotgun hands-down.

The rare weapons (Ivory Bow, etc.) are balanced by: cost/lack of Manuver/
or uniqueness.

I know of no other collectable card game that strives so hard for the
game balance over gotta-buy-more-cards-so-I-can-win syndrome.

L. Scott
